title: Maximum-entropy IRL and a GAIL discriminator
brief: Recover a reward that explains an expert on a grid world by matching feature counts, then build the discriminator loss and reward that GAIL trains a policy with.
hints: In soft_value_iteration, loop t from T - 1 down to 0. Q = r[:, None] + P @ V[t + 1] has shape (S, A). Take a stable logsumexp over axis 1 by subtracting each row's max first.
The policy is pi[t] = exp(Q - V[t][:, None]). If a row does not sum to one, V[t] is not the logsumexp of that same Q.
state_visitation is one einsum per step: np.einsum('s,sa,sap->p', D[t], pi[t], P). D has T rows, not T + 1, because the last reward is paid at step T - 1.
maxent_irl_gradient is f_expert minus feature_expectations of the visitation under the soft-optimal policy for r = features @ theta. The sign matters: gradient ascent adds it.
For discriminator_loss, log sigmoid(z) = -np.logaddexp(0, -z) and log(1 - sigmoid(z)) = -np.logaddexp(0, z). The gradient is rho_policy * D - rho_expert * (1 - D).
